questions.q: What is terraform import used for?
options: Bringing a real resource that already exists under Terraform's management without recreating it
Downloading a provider plugin from the Terraform Registry
Converting Bicep templates into HCL automatically
Copying one project's state file into another project
questions.explain: Import is for infrastructure created by hand or another tool that you now want Terraform to track and manage.

questions.q: What does terraform import actually do to the real cloud resource it's pointed at?
options: It recreates the resource under a new ID
It modifies the resource's tags to mark it as Terraform-managed
It deletes and immediately rebuilds the resource
Nothing — it only reads the resource and records it in state
questions.explain: Import writes to terraform.tfstate only — it never creates, modifies, or destroys anything in the real world.

questions.q: In the correct import workflow, what should you do before running terraform import?
options: Write a resource block in your .tf config matching what you believe the real resource looks like
Nothing is needed beforehand — import writes the config block for you automatically
Delete any existing state file so import has a clean slate
Run terraform destroy on the target resource first
questions.explain: Import has no idea what your .tf files say, so the resource block needs to exist (or be generated) for the workflow to make sense.

questions.q: You run terraform import successfully but never add a matching resource block to your config. What does the next terraform plan show?
options: An error that permanently locks the state file
That the resource will be destroyed, because it exists in state but isn't declared in configuration
No changes at all, since import already finished the job
A warning that is safe to ignore indefinitely
questions.explain: Terraform reconciles config against state; a resource in state with no matching config block reads as 'remove this.'

questions.q: What does the Terraform 1.5+ -generate-config-out flag do?
options: Exports your state file into Bicep syntax
Writes a best-guess resource block from an imported object's real attributes for you to review
Automatically fixes any plan that would destroy an orphaned resource
Generates a new provider block based on your cloud account
questions.explain: It's a convenience for the config-writing step, not a replacement for reviewing and reconciling the result with plan.
